text: Add a categorical tab-by-hour interaction feature to the additive scorer.
rationale: The current context-aware scorer has strong overall within-user discrimination (GAUC 0.668912) but weak top-five results in several large hour slices, including hour 16 nDCG@5 0.357042 and hour 14 nDCG@5 0.363601. A single causal context conjunction can model time-of-surface effects that separate tab and hour weights cannot express.
exact_ablation: Add exactly one train-vocabulary categorical feature formed as the tuple (tab, hour) to experiment 1's existing additive user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday scorer; retain the model, binary loss, optimizer, regularization, seed, and training schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.000 to +0.003 versus experiment 1, because tab-specific time effects may repair within-user inversions.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.005 versus experiment 1, with greater potential than GAUC because the diagnosed deficit is concentrated at top five in context slices.

text: Add a categorical tab-by-weekday interaction feature to the additive scorer.
rationale: Request context was the only positively screened feature family before experiment 1, while official validation shows substantial heterogeneity by tab. A tab-weekday term is an independently interpretable extension of the already permitted request-time context.
exact_ablation: Add exactly one train-vocabulary categorical feature formed as the tuple (tab, weekday) to experiment 1's existing feature set; keep all existing fields, additive architecture, BCE loss, optimizer, regularization, seed, and training schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.002 versus experiment 1; broad weekly effects may be weak after tab and weekday main effects.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.000 to +0.004 versus experiment 1 if weekly surface mixes alter the highest-ranked impressions.

text: Replace scalar additive field weights with a second-order factorization-machine scorer over the unchanged allowed fields.
rationale: Experiment 1 is limited to additive contributions from user, video, and request-context categories. Its GAUC 0.668912 confirms nontrivial ordering signal, while tab 0 and tab 6 have very low nDCG@5 despite context being present, indicating that user/item/context interactions may be missing rather than additional feature families.
exact_ablation: Replace experiment 1's additive scalar-weight scorer with a second-order factorization machine using exactly the same five fields (user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday), while preserving BCE, train/validation splits, optimizer settings, regularization strength, seed, and early-stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.006 versus experiment 1 from learned user-video and item-context interactions.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.007 versus experiment 1 if those interactions promote long-view candidates into the top five.

text: Replace the additive scorer with an embedding-plus-MLP pointwise ranker over the unchanged allowed fields.
rationale: The current model has one scalar parameter per categorical value and cannot represent nonlinear combinations. Official validation demonstrates usable signal overall but pronounced context-specific top-five weakness, especially tab 0 nDCG@5 0.062187 and tab 6 nDCG@5 0.105841.
exact_ablation: Replace experiment 1's additive scalar-weight architecture with an embedding-plus-MLP architecture consuming exactly user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday; preserve the BCE objective, temporal splits, optimizer family, training seed, and early-stopping criterion.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.008 versus experiment 1 through nonlinear identity-context score variation within users.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.009 versus experiment 1 if nonlinear interactions correct top-ranked item ordering.

text: Use a two-layer Deep & Cross scorer over the unchanged allowed fields.
rationale: The baseline's additive representation cannot encode bounded-order interactions among user ID, video ID, and request context. This is relevant because request context was the only screened positive family and tab slices have large ranking disparities, including tab 8 GAUC 0.351852 and nDCG@5 0.026336.
exact_ablation: Replace experiment 1's additive architecture with a two-layer Deep & Cross scorer using embeddings for exactly user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday; retain BCE, all data processing, temporal splits, and the existing training schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.000 to +0.007 versus experiment 1 from explicit bounded-order feature interactions.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.008 versus experiment 1 if context-conditioned item interactions improve top-five swaps.

text: Increase only L2 regularization on the existing additive scorer.
rationale: The validation model is dominated by warm items (121510 of 124909 rows) while rare and cold item slices have much lower nDCG@5. Stronger shrinkage can reduce overconfident memorization of sparse IDs without introducing any new feature or leakage pathway.
exact_ablation: Change only the additive model's L2 coefficient from 1e-6 to 1e-5; preserve fields, architecture, loss, optimizer, learning rate, seed, batches, and stopping schedule from experiment 1.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.002 versus experiment 1; regularization may reduce sparse-ID overfit but can also underfit frequent IDs.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.003 versus experiment 1, with possible benefit in sparse-item ordering but limited expected global movement.

text: Replace Adam with AdaGrad for the unchanged additive scorer.
rationale: The model contains high-cardinality user and video parameters with highly unequal update frequencies. Official diagnostics show a sharp gap between warm-item nDCG@5 0.537042 and medium-item nDCG@5 0.244907, so a frequency-adaptive optimizer is a bounded optimization test without adding unverified features.
exact_ablation: Replace Adam with AdaGrad in experiment 1's existing additive model, leaving the five fields, BCE loss, initial learning rate, L2 coefficient, seed, batch size, and stopping rule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.002 to +0.003 versus experiment 1; frequency-adaptive updates may improve sparse-parameter fitting but could slow dense-parameter learning.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.002 to +0.003 versus experiment 1, with any gain expected mainly from improved ordering on less-frequent items.

text: Train the unchanged additive scorer with inverse training-user impression-count weighted BCE.
rationale: GAUC is computed from within-user AUCs, but ordinary row-level BCE lets users with more training impressions contribute more gradient mass. The current user-frequency slices differ modestly in outcomes, while user-level ranking is the official target; user-normalized supervision is a direct alignment test.
exact_ablation: Replace unweighted row-level BCE with BCE weighted by the inverse number of impressions for each user in the training split only, normalized to mean weight one; keep features, architecture, optimizer, learning rate, L2, seed, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.000 to +0.004 versus experiment 1 by reducing gradient domination from highly represented users.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.003 versus experiment 1 because user balancing is not explicitly top-five oriented.

text: Add a fixed-weight within-user RankNet pairwise term to the existing BCE objective.
rationale: Experiment 1 already achieves GAUC 0.668912 but has nDCG@5 0.536958, with especially weak top-five rankings in major tabs. A pairwise term directly trains positive impressions above negative impressions for the same user, targeting the within-user ordering used by GAUC without introducing features.
exact_ablation: Add exactly one auxiliary RankNet logistic pairwise loss over positive-negative pairs from the same training user, with fixed loss L=BCE+0.25*RankNet; retain experiment 1's fields, additive scorer, optimizer, regularization, seed, and training schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.006 versus experiment 1 because the added term optimizes within-user positive-negative order.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.000 to +0.005 versus experiment 1; it may improve top-five placement, but uniformly sampled pairs can emphasize non-top-rank errors.

text: Replace BCE with a mixed-user ListNet top-one objective.
rationale: The most conspicuous official weakness is nDCG@5 in tab slices rather than uniform absence of discrimination. A listwise loss over complete training-user candidate sets is a direct, high-information test of whether top-of-list competition is the limiting factor.
exact_ablation: Replace experiment 1's BCE objective with a ListNet top-one loss computed only over mixed-label candidate sets formed by all training impressions of each user within each calendar day; keep the five allowed fields, additive architecture, optimizer, regularization, seed, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.002 to +0.003 versus experiment 1, since listwise normalization may not preserve all pairwise orderings.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.007 versus experiment 1 if same-day per-user candidate competition resembles the top-five evaluation errors.

text: Add adversarial embedding regularization to an embedding factorization-machine replacement scorer.
rationale: Sparse entity segments are substantially weaker than warm items, and a robustness intervention can regularize learned user/video representations without relying on prohibited outcome fields or quarantined snapshots. This candidate is intentionally a robustness-oriented alternative to pure capacity expansion.
exact_ablation: Replace experiment 1's additive scorer with an embedding factorization-machine scorer trained with one additional adversarial embedding-loss term on user_id and video_id embeddings only, using a fixed perturbation radius equal to 3% of the median training-batch embedding norm and loss weight 0.25; retain the same five fields and BCE base loss.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.002 to +0.004 versus experiment 1; robustness can help sparse representations but may constrain useful personalization.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.002 to +0.004 versus experiment 1, with uncertain benefit because adversarial training does not explicitly target rank five.

text: Average logits from three independently seeded instances of the unchanged additive scorer.
rationale: The positive request-context screening lift was small relative to daily variation, so optimization variance is a credible risk. Averaging independent models can stabilize rankings without adding features, while experiment 1 supplies the measured reference score and the relevant score distribution.
exact_ablation: Replace experiment 1's single-model inference with the arithmetic mean of raw logits from exactly three independently initialized and shuffled copies of the identical experiment 1 model, trained with seeds 0, 1, and 2 and otherwise identical configuration.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.000 to +0.003 versus experiment 1 through lower optimization variance.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.000 to +0.004 versus experiment 1 if averaging resolves near-tied top-five scores; gains may be negligible because the additive model is low variance.
